inputs.title: Oscillator
inputs.tooltip:
Built-in choices (RSI, Stochastic, CCI, MACD) set the Scaling Mode, Low / High and Max levels automatically to that indicator's standard values. Those settings are greyed out.
Choose External Source to use any indicator on the chart and set them yourself.

Pine cannot read the name of the plot you pick above, so type a short name here (for example: MACD Hist, ADX, VARSI). It shows in the Info Panel as External Source | <name>. Leave empty to show External Source only.
inputs.title: Source Name (for Info Panel)

inputs.tooltip:
Bounded = the oscillator has fixed limits (RSI 0..100, Stochastic 0..100, EVEREX -100..+100). Set Low / High to those limits.
Unbounded = no fixed limits (MACD, CCI, Momentum, Volume). The script finds the limits itself from the last N bars (Lookback).

One Direction = blocks grow from a baseline in one direction only (Up or Down, see 'One Direction: Draw').
Centered / Zero-Centered = values above the center line draw up, values below it draw down.

Examples:
RSI, Stochastic -> Bounded - Centered (0 / 100, center 50)
EVEREX -> Bounded - Centered (-100 / +100, center 0)
MACD Histogram, Momentum -> Unbounded - Zero-Centered
ADX, Aroon -> Bounded - One Direction, Up (0 / 100)
Drawdown % from high -> Bounded - One Direction, Down (-100 / 0)
Volume, ATR -> Unbounded - One Direction, Up
inputs.title: Scaling Mode
One Direction: Draw
inputs.tooltip:
Used only by the two One Direction modes.
Up: the baseline is at Low and blocks grow upward as the value rises.
Down: the baseline is at High and blocks grow downward as the value falls (for example, drawdown from a high: 0 down to -100%).

inputs.title: Unbounded: Lookback (bars)
inputs.tooltip:
Lookback above 1: the full block height is the largest value seen in the last N bars (the scale adapts to recent history).
Lookback = 1: no lookback, real values. Each block is a fixed size (Block Size below), so the blocks line up with the oscillator's own values and Pane Scale = Match Oscillator works.

Value of one block, in the oscillator's own units, used when Lookback = 1.
Example: MACD Histogram with Block Size 0.2 and 10 bands -> full height = 2.0. Volume with Block Size 500000 -> full height = 5,000,000.
inputs.title: Unbounded: Block Size (when Lookback = 1)

inputs.tooltip:
Match Oscillator: the blocks are drawn in the oscillator's own units (for RSI 0..100 the center line is at 50), so the original oscillator can be placed on the same pane and scale. Works with the two Bounded modes, and with the Unbounded modes when Lookback = 1.
Block Units: each block is 1 unit and the center line is at 0. Unbounded modes with Lookback above 1 always use Block Units.
inputs.title: Pane Scale

inputs.tooltip:
By Level (horizontal): each block level has its color (bottom to top).
By Value (vertical): the whole column takes the color of its top block.
inputs.title: Color Mode
Peak Hold Bars
inputs.tooltip:
Peak Hold marks the highest block reached in recent bars, like the small marker on a music equalizer.
When the value drops, the marker stays at the old high for the number of Hold Bars, then falls one block per bar until it meets the current level.
It shows how strong the move was a moment ago, compared with now.
Brightness of the block nearest the center line. The outer block is always full brightness. Higher value = brighter center blocks. 5-7 works well on dark charts.
inputs.title: Center Block Brightness (1 - 10)
Range Contrast (0.1 to 3.0)
inputs.tooltip:
Controls the contrast range from Weak to Strong.
1.0 = even steps.
Above 1 = Bigger range = lower blocks stay closer to the Weak color, only the top blocks are bright.
Below 1 = blocks become bright sooner.

Enter the level in the oscillator's own units (RSI 70, MACD 2.0, Volume 5000000).
Alert: the oscillator crosses ABOVE this level. Works like an RSI overbought line.
inputs.title: Input 29

inputs.tooltip:
Enter the level in the oscillator's own units (RSI 30, MACD -2.0).
Alert: the oscillator crosses BELOW this level. Works like an RSI oversold line.
inputs.title: Input 31

inputs.id: Show Flip Markers on Price Chart
inputs.title: Show Flip Markers on Price Chart
inputs.tooltip:
Flip Up: the oscillator crosses above the baseline.
Flip Down: the oscillator crosses below the baseline.
The baseline is the center line (Centered modes) or the floor / ceiling (One Direction modes).
